international.canonicalTopic: Flood-management pressures in Thailand’s Chao Phraya basin
international.headline: Thailand’s flood-diversion strategy leaves downstream communities exposed

facts: The report described recurring monsoon floods in communities in Ayutthaya province, downstream of infrastructure intended to protect Bangkok and industrial areas along the Chao Phraya River.

national.canonicalTopic: Additional MGNREGA work for Forest Rights Act title holders
national.headline: No order yet on additional workdays for Forest Rights Act title holders under the new rural employment law
group1: Group 1 Paper III: Polity, Governance, Ethics
facts: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, guarantees 125 days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year and has no separate entitlement tier for Forest Rights Act title holders.

national.canonicalTopic: Supreme Court safeguards on communication of arrest grounds
national.headline: Supreme Court sets requirements for communicating grounds of arrest and re-arrest
facts: In Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab (September 2026), the Supreme Court said an investigating agency seeking to re-arrest an accused after an earlier arrest was held illegal for failure to provide written grounds must obtain the magistrate’s permission.
The application must explain why the grounds were not supplied, be made after those grounds have been furnished to the accused, and carry the immediate superior authority’s endorsement.
The Court called for the investigation to be transferred to another officer and for a departmental inquiry into the investigating officer’s lapse.

The article reports that the Court required grounds of arrest to be communicated in writing, in a language understood by the accused, at least two hours before remand proceedings; non-compliance renders the arrest and remand illegal.
national.summary: The Supreme Court’s ruling addresses communication of arrest grounds and the consequences of failing to meet that safeguard, including the procedure for a subsequent re-arrest.
national.staticLink: Article 22 of the Constitution; Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Article 22 protects an arrested person’s rights; the article identifies Section 47 of the BNSS as the statutory duty to communicate grounds of arrest.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how procedural safeguards at arrest protect personal liberty and what institutional accountability should follow their breach.

sources.title: How has the SC strengthened arrest safeguards?

national.notes:
# 1. Communicating grounds of arrest
- **Case:** **Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab**, **September 2026**.
- **Court:** **Supreme Court of India**.
- **Requirement:** Grounds of arrest must be communicated in writing, in a language understood by the accused, at least **two hours** before remand proceedings.
- **Consequence:** Non-compliance renders the arrest and remand illegal.
- **Legal basis cited:** **Article 22** of the Constitution; **Section 47** of the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS)**.
# 2. Procedure for re-arrest
- **Permission:** If an earlier arrest was held illegal because written grounds were not provided, the investigating agency must obtain the magistrate’s permission to re-arrest.
- **Application requirements:** Explain why the grounds were not supplied; be made after the grounds have been furnished to the accused; carry the immediate superior authority’s endorsement.
- **Further directions:** Transfer the investigation to another officer and hold a departmental inquiry into the investigating officer’s lapse.
> Exam angle: Test the written-grounds safeguard, **two-hour** timing and magistrate-permission requirements for re-arrest.

andhraPradesh.headline: Northeast Monsoon may bring rain to Andhra Pradesh through October 19
facts: The report relayed a forecast of a wet spell in Andhra Pradesh from October 14 to 19, 2026, with Northeast Monsoon onset over South Peninsular India expected from October 15.
Light to moderate showers and isolated heavy rain were forecast across Rayalaseema, South Coastal Andhra and North Coastal Andhra from October 16 to 19.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra secures first-innings lead as its Ranji match against Karnataka ends in a draw
facts: Andhra and Karnataka drew their Ranji Trophy match at the ACA Stadium in Mulapadu, Andhra Pradesh.
Andhra made 418 in its first innings; Karnataka scored 274 and 337/9 declared in its two innings.
Andhra finished its second innings at 104/4 while pursuing a target of 194; its first-innings lead earned it three points, while Karnataka received one point.
Andhra bowler Lalith Mohan took five wickets for 117 runs in Karnataka’s second innings; Karun Nair scored 155 not out for Karnataka.
